title: arXiv Mathematics — daily notable papers (2 October 2026)
global_caveat: This is an inferred editorial ranking, not an official arXiv trending chart; these papers are only days old, so citation and attention evidence is too limited to support a popularity ranking.

sections.abstract: The authors prove that the planar critical Ising magnetization scaling-limit field is measurable from the nested CLE_3 spin-interface ensemble, complementing an earlier construction from colored CLE_{16/3}.
sections.claimed_result: Reconstruction of the critical Ising magnetization field from nested CLE_3; the route through CLE percolation to colored CLE_{16/3} recovers the same field.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical planar Ising scaling limits on a sufficiently regular domain; the introduction describes + boundary conditions and the nested interface limit.
sections.unique_caveat: The converse—that nested CLE_3 can be reconstructed from the magnetization field—is explicitly conjectured, not proved.
sections.title: The critical Ising magnetization field can be reconstructed from its +/- interfaces

sections.abstract: Using entropy, the authors bound the number of rainbow triangles in an r-edge-coloured graph with m edges by C_r m^(3/2), where C_r = sqrt(2(r-2)/(9r)), establish sharpness when an affine plane of order r−1 exists, and give a stability statement; they also study properly coloured larger cliques.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the stated rainbow-triangle upper bound and show near-extremizers must reflect affine-plane structure; for odd r, blowups of a properly edge-coloured K_{r+1} maximize the larger-clique count.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Simple graph with m edges and r≥3 edge colours; the triangle bound is sharp under the stated affine-plane condition.
sections.unique_caveat: Sharpness depends on existence of the relevant plane; the abstract does not give a universal exact improvement when it does not exist.
sections.title: On Colorful Kruskal--Katona Theorems

sections.abstract: For small quadratic regularization, the authors describe the support geometry and potential expansions of optimal transport couplings, and prove sharp L^p approximation rates for two estimators of the Brenier map.
sections.claimed_result: Under the paper’s assumptions, the support contains the Brenier-map graph for sufficiently small regularization; rescaled sections have ellipsoidal interior and half-space boundary limits, with sharp L^p rates and leading biases for two map approximations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Quadratic cost and quadratic regularization; marginals have positive C^{1,α} densities on bounded uniformly convex supports with C^{3,α} boundaries, bounded above and away from zero.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorems rely on substantial smoothness and uniform convexity; transfer to rough, degenerate, or nonconvex settings is not established by this paper’s stated assumptions.
sections.title: Geometry and Convergence of Quadratically Regularized Optimal Transport II

sections.abstract: The authors extend the linear-arboricity conjecture to infinite graphs of finite maximum degree, prove equivalence of its finite and infinite versions, and bound a related topological linear arboricity for high-girth regular graphs.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show finite and infinite versions of the conjecture are equivalent; their new topological variant differs from linear arboricity by at most one, and every 2k-regular graph of girth at least 2k has topological linear arboricity at most k+1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Infinite graphs are required to have finite maximum degree; the final bound assumes 2k-regularity and girth at least 2k.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not claim an unconditional resolution of the underlying finite Linear Arboricity Conjecture; it establishes equivalence and related bounds.
sections.title: Linear arboricity conjecture for infinite graphs

sections.abstract: The authors study vector balancing when each vector can be signed and its coordinates permuted, proving explicit bounds for the balancing and prefix problems and asymptotic optimality in dimension by a geometric method.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove explicit bounds for both the signed-permutation vector-balancing problem and its prefix variant, and show the bound is asymptotically optimal in dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Vectors may each receive a sign and a coordinate permutation; the abstract does not specify the detailed norm or exact bound.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract omits the formula and detailed hypotheses, so the constant and the precise range of the optimality statement require reading the full paper.
sections.title: An optimal constant for vector balancing with permutations

sections.abstract: The author reports an improved error term in the prime geodesic theorem for the modular group and extends the result to congruence subgroups of indefinite quaternion algebras over Q.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims an improved error term for the modular-group prime geodesic theorem, applicable more generally to congruence subgroups of indefinite quaternion algebras over Q.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Prime geodesic counting for the modular group and the stated congruence subgroups of indefinite quaternion algebras over Q.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state the old and new error exponents, so the quantitative size of the improvement cannot be assessed from the abstract alone.
sections.title: On the prime geodesic theorem
